report.tagline: Once India's most valuable startup, an online learning app for school students that grew on hard selling and debt, and has been in insolvency since 2024.
report.simpleSummary: BYJU'S was an app with animated video lessons for school students, from Class 1 to exam prep. Sales teams called parents and pushed year-long courses that cost ₹30,000 to ₹1 lakh or more, often paid with loans. It used investor money and a $1.2 billion loan to buy other companies and sponsor the Indian cricket team. When schools reopened after COVID, sales fell, losses piled up, it could not pay its debts, and an Indian court put it into insolvency in 2024. In 2026 the company is run by a resolution professional, not its founder.

overview.whatItDoes: BYJU'S sold online courses for school students, with pre-recorded animated lessons, quizzes and later live tutoring classes. It also owned other learning companies: Aakash (offline test prep), WhiteHat Jr (coding for kids), Great Learning (adult upskilling) and Epic (US reading app). Today it is in a corporate insolvency resolution process, and its main brands are being sold or fought over by lenders.
howItWorks: Parents downloaded the free app and gave a phone number.
Sales staff called or visited homes to sell year-long or multi-year course packages, often with a tablet.
Many parents paid through no-cost EMI loans from partner lenders, so they owed money even if the child stopped using the app.
Students watched animated lessons and took adaptive quizzes; BYJU'S Classes added live tutoring.
The company used investor money and debt to buy companies and expand abroad.
overview.valueProposition: Engaging, well-made lessons at home that helped children understand concepts, not just memorise them. The weakness was that the price and the selling method did not match the value most families got.

painPoints.pain: Children find school maths and science hard to understand from textbooks.
painPoints.howSolved: Animated video lessons that showed concepts visually.

painPoints.pain: Good tutors are expensive or unavailable in smaller towns.
painPoints.howSolved: Lessons from well-known teachers on any phone or tablet.

painPoints.pain: During COVID, schools closed and parents needed learning at home.
painPoints.howSolved: Large library of self-paced content plus live classes.

painPoints.pain: Parents cannot track what their child is learning.
painPoints.howSolved: Progress reports and quiz scores in the app.

painPoints.pain: Paying ₹50,000 upfront is hard for many families.
painPoints.howSolved: EMI loans through partner lenders. This solved the payment pain but created a bigger debt pain for many families.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Animated video lessons and quizzes from Class 1 to 12 and exam prep.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The actual product. Many parents and students did like the lessons.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Free sessions and content that collected parents' phone numbers.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Fed a huge sales team with leads. This was the real growth engine.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Sales staff sold high-priced packages, often financed by loans.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Pushed revenue up fast but led to complaints, refunds and a reputation crisis.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Live online tutoring and later physical tuition centres after COVID.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: An attempt to add real teaching when recorded videos alone were not enough.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Aakash, WhiteHat Jr, Great Learning, Epic, Toppr and others.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Bought growth but added cost and debt; Aakash became the most valuable asset left.

businessModel.summary: BYJU'S made money by selling expensive course packages upfront, using a large sales team. Revenue depended on a constant supply of new buyers, because many did not renew. When COVID ended, new sales fell and the high fixed costs and debt sank the company.

revenueStreams.detail: One-time or multi-year packages, often ₹30,000 to ₹1 lakh plus, many financed by EMI loans.

revenueStreams.stream: Test prep (Aakash and BYJU'S exam prep)
revenueStreams.detail: Aakash offline coaching became the largest and steadiest revenue source.

revenueStreams.stream: Coding and upskilling (WhiteHat Jr, Great Learning)
revenueStreams.detail: Paid classes for kids' coding and adult courses.
US subscriptions for reading and maths apps; Epic was sold off in US bankruptcy.

businessModel.pricing: Not public as a fixed list. Packages were sold one-to-one by sales staff, often ₹30,000 to ₹1 lakh or more, according to news and parent complaints.
costDrivers: A very large sales force paid on targets
Celebrity and sports sponsorship, including BCCI and FIFA World Cup
Interest on the $1.2 billion term loan
Acquisition costs and running many separate companies
businessModel.unitEconomics: Imagine one family buys a ₹60,000 package. To win that sale, BYJU'S paid for TV ads, many free trials, calls and home visits, and a commission to the salesperson, which together could take a large part of that ₹60,000. Revenue was also often counted before the service was delivered, which auditors later questioned. If the child stops using the app and does not renew, BYJU'S never earns a second payment to make back its CAC (the cost to win that customer). The model only worked while new sales kept rising.

howTheyGetUsers: Free app content to collect parent leads
Large outbound sales teams with tough targets
Buying other companies to add users and revenue
whatBringsUsersBack: Daily lessons and quizzes for engaged students
In practice, retention was weak for many families after the first months
growth.moat: BYJU'S had strong brand awareness and good content, but neither was hard to copy. Cheaper rivals like Physics Wallah offered good teaching for a fraction of the price, and free YouTube content was everywhere. Without high retention or low costs, there was no real moat.

competitors.name: Physics Wallah
competitors.positioning: Low-price coaching with free YouTube content and offline centres.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: PW priced at a few thousand rupees a year and grew from organic YouTube reach; BYJU'S charged ten times more and relied on paid marketing and sales.

competitors.name: Vedantu
competitors.positioning: Live online tutoring for K-12 and exam prep.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Vedantu focused on live classes; BYJU'S on recorded animated content plus sales.

competitors.name: Unacademy
competitors.positioning: Subscription test-prep platform with many educators.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Unacademy sold monthly or yearly subscriptions online; BYJU'S sold larger packages door to door.

competitors.name: Local tuition teachers
competitors.positioning: The default for most Indian families.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Tuition is personal and cheap; BYJU'S was scalable but impersonal and expensive.

northStar.metric: Students actively learning each week (should have been). In practice BYJU'S chased new sales bookings.
northStar.why: Learning only happens if a child keeps using the product. Tracking bookings instead hid that many paying families had stopped using the app, which later showed up as refunds, complaints and no renewals.

improvementIdeas.idea: Replace upfront packages with a monthly subscription that can be cancelled any time
improvementIdeas.problem: Parents locked into loans for products their children stopped using.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer complaints and refunds, and revenue that reflects real usage.

improvementIdeas.idea: Pay sales staff on 90-day student activity, not on signed contracts
improvementIdeas.problem: Sales incentives rewarded closing deals, not student learning.

improvementIdeas.idea: Weekly study plan with a live teacher check-in
improvementIdeas.problem: Recorded videos alone led to low usage after a few weeks.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher week-4 activity and more renewals.

improvementIdeas.idea: Focus the business on Aakash and sell or close unrelated units
improvementIdeas.problem: Too many companies, too much debt.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Lower fixed costs and a business that can survive.

pmLessons: Sales can create revenue, but only product value creates retention. If users stop using what they bought, growth will reverse.
Growth bought with debt and ads hides weak unit economics until the money runs out.
A temporary boom, like COVID school closures, is not a lasting market. Plan for demand to return to normal.
Trust is a product feature. Mis-selling and refund fights destroyed the brand faster than any competitor could.
Governance matters for product teams too: if numbers are not trusted, investors, lenders and customers leave.

interviewQuestions.question: Why did BYJU'S fail, in one minute?
interviewQuestions.hint: Structure as: weak retention, very high CAC, debt-funded acquisitions, post-COVID demand drop, governance failures. End with one lesson.

interviewQuestions.question: If you were the PM at BYJU'S in 2021, what one metric would you have pushed leadership to track?
interviewQuestions.hint: Argue for active learners or 90-day retention over bookings, and explain how it would have revealed the problem early.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you redesign BYJU'S pricing for a small-town family?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare upfront packages, monthly plans and freemium. Use Physics Wallah's low price as a benchmark and discuss CAC payback.

interviewQuestions.question: Physics Wallah succeeded where BYJU'S failed. What is the core difference?
interviewQuestions.hint: Organic acquisition vs paid sales, low price vs high price, teachers vs animation, profitability focus vs growth at all costs.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you rebuild trust with parents after a mis-selling scandal?
interviewQuestions.hint: Easy cancellation, transparent pricing, refund guarantees, usage-based sales incentives, and public metrics on complaints.

glossary.meaning: When a company cannot pay its debts and a court-led process decides what happens to it.
India's legal process where a resolution professional runs a failing company and creditors vote on a rescue or sale plan.
A large loan from institutional investors, usually repaid in one lump at the end.
Customer acquisition cost: how much it costs to win one paying customer.
Equated monthly instalment: paying for something in fixed monthly loan payments.
How many customers keep using or paying for a product over time.
How much money a business makes or loses on one customer or one sale.
Net promoter score: a survey score showing how likely customers are to recommend you.
What investors think a whole company is worth.
Something that makes it hard for competitors to copy or beat a business.

assumptions: Package price range of ₹30,000 to ₹1 lakh is based on news reports and parent complaints, not an official price list.
The unit economics example is illustrative; BYJU'S never published CAC or per-customer profit.
The $533 million moved through the US unit comes from US court filings as widely reported, not from a source listed above.
The outcome of the June 2026 resolution plan deadline was not found in sources; the process may have moved on since.
